trust_decision.summary: Whether a path-scoped middleware (e.g. auth via MiddlewareConsumer.forRoutes or app.use(path, fn)) runs for a request is decided by matching the request target against the middleware path, in two sequential gates: the vendored middie engine's prefix regexp and the FastifyAdapter's per-route regexp on sanitizeUrl(originalUrl); neither strips an absolute-form target (http://host/path) while the Fastify router (find-my-way) does, so the handler runs without the middleware.

landing_point.why: The summary names @nestjs/platform-fastify and path-scoped middleware; FastifyAdapter.sanitizeUrl is the visible path normalizer called from createMiddlewareFactory (fastify-adapter.ts:745) right before the route regexp check.

fix_sites.entry_point: MiddlewareConsumer.apply(...).forRoutes(...) -> FastifyAdapter.createMiddlewareFactory callback (fastify-adapter.ts:745); fix adds getPathFromRequestTarget (fix.diff:979-983, fix.diff:997-1016)

app.use(path, fn) via FastifyAdapter.use (fastify-adapter.ts:775-783) and every forRoutes middleware via this.instance.use (fastify-adapter.ts:736); prefix gate at fastify-middie.ts:189. Fix deletes the vendored engine and switches to @fastify/middie 9.3.4 (fix.diff:919, fix.diff:927, fix.diff:1018-1023, fix.diff:1207-1212)
fix_sites.module_kind: vendored clone of third-party library (second implementation)

fix_sites.entry_point: new FastifyAdapter({ ignoreTrailingSlash, ignoreDuplicateSlashes, caseSensitive, ... }) public constructor; fix folds top-level router options into routerOptions via getTopLevelRouterOptions (fix.diff:931-943, fix.diff:954-972)
FastifyAdapter.init / createMiddlewareFactory -> registerMiddie (plugin registration switched to upstream package, fix.diff:919)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: packages/platform-fastify/adapters/middie/fastify-middie.ts:109-114 and packages/platform-fastify/adapters/middie/fastify-middie.ts:189 (vendored @fastify/middie clone; its prefix regexp gates every middleware before the adapter's own check runs)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The middie file is labelled 'A clone of @fastify/middie engine' (packages/platform-fastify/adapters/middie/fastify-middie.ts:44-48), so a solver can treat it as third-party code and only patch FastifyAdapter.sanitizeUrl, yet that gate rejects absolute-form first, so the middleware stays skipped.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Origin-form paths that contain '://' or no leading-slash quirks (e.g. /redirect/http://x), non-http(s) schemes and malformed authority-only targets must be left untouched, query/hash stripping must keep working, and absolute-form requests (legitimate per RFC 9112, sent by proxies) must still be served and not rejected; a fix that runs new URL() on every url or 400s absolute-form breaks these. Route exclusions (.exclude) also match on the raw URL.

O6_input_shapes: absolute-form combined with duplicate slashes, trailing slash and upper-case path under ignoreDuplicateSlashes/ignoreTrailingSlash/caseSensitive=false
router options given top-level vs under routerOptions

O7_producer.where: packages/platform-fastify/adapters/fastify-adapter.ts:260-268 builds the Fastify options whose initialConfig both gates read (fastify-adapter.ts:936-938, fastify-middie.ts:163-187)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Exclusion path extraction for middleware .exclude() uses raw getRequestUrl; a planted variant that resolves absolute-form here but not in a gate (or vice versa) creates a parser differential on the protected path's identity.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer fixing 'exclude does not work behind a forward proxy' would naturally normalize only this helper in core, platform-agnostic, without touching the fastify gates.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: getRequestOriginalUrl/getRequestUrl returns the raw request target; a sibling consumer (e.g. a prefix-based guard or global-prefix 404 routing) matching on it would be bypassable the same way.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getRequestUrl is the documented platform-agnostic URL accessor (packages/common/interfaces/http/http-server.interface.ts:481-487), so core code plausibly path-matches on it.

O9_family: authentication bypass via path-normalization parser differential between middleware matcher and router (CWE-288/CWE-436)

O10_build.toolchain: npm install at repo root, tsc build of packages; tests via vitest (integration/hello-world/e2e)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strip scheme/authority in FastifyAdapter.sanitizeUrl only, leaving the vendored middie prefix gate (fastify-middie.ts:189) rejecting absolute-form before the adapter callback ever runs.

out_of_scope_notes: platform-express path-scoped middleware relies on Express's own URL parsing; not checked for absolute-form handling.
Core route exclusion (packages/core/middleware/utils.ts:119-136) matches on the raw URL; with absolute-form it fails closed (middleware runs), a correctness gap rather than a bypass.

Whether Fastify 5.12.x initialConfig exposes top-level ignoreTrailingSlash/caseSensitive: node_modules absent, so it is unknown if getTopLevelRouterOptions is needed at the pinned commit, where both gates already read top-level keys, or only for the upstream middie switch.

Exact absolute-form handling inside @fastify/middie 9.3.4 and find-my-way 9.9.0 not read (not in tree); the claim that find-my-way strips absolute-form is taken from the fix's comment (fix.diff:992-996).
